item.title: Commercial Chartering Services by Shipping Ministry liable to service tax on 1% commission, Extended Limitation Period Not Applicable: CESTAT
item.description: The Tribunal found no intent to evade and a bona fide belief of non-taxability, it limited the demand to the normal period with interest and waived all penalties under Section 80.

item.title: Premium Earned from Transfer of Sugar Export Quota Not Taxable as Service: CESTAT Holds Transaction is Sale of Goods, Not BAS [Read Order]
item.description: The tribunal held that transfer of export quota constitutes sale of goods and no taxable service was rendered in such transactions

item.title: Vehicle Registered in Puducherry but used in Kerala: Kerala HC upholds ₹15.37 Lakh Motor Vehicle Tax Demand
item.description: The Kerala High Court upheld a Rs. 15.37 lakh motor vehicle tax demand after finding that a car registered in Puducherry was in fact used only in Kerala.

item.title: Commercial Tribunal allows ITC Solely on Seller’s Registration Ignoring Core Finding of Circular Money Transactions: Allahabad HC Remands Matter [Read Order]
item.description: Allahabad HC quashes tribunal’s order allowing ITC based only on seller registration after observing that the Tribunal ignored the Assessing Officer’s finding of circular money transactions.

item.title: Supreme Court Orders SBI, PNB to Clarify Loan Status After Man Alleges Wrongful Negative CIBIL Score [Read Order]
item.description: The petitioner claimed he had no loans or defaults, yet his credit profile reflected negative scoring due to a PAN number shared by two other individuals with the same name.

item.title: Non-Resident Individual Tax Guide for AY 2025-26: Understanding Residential Status, Tax Regimes, and Available Deductions
item.description: This Article summarizes NRI tax rules for AY 2025–26, including residential status, applicable ITR forms, and the new tax regimes. It also highlighted major deductions available under each regime to help NRIs optimize tax liability and ensure compliance.

item.title: NCLAT Distinguishes Fraudulent Trading from Wrongful Trading Provisions [Read Order]
item.description: SUMMARY: The tribunal explained that fraudulent trading can be established without proving "twilight-of-insolvency" timing if business was carried on with intent to defraud creditors, whereas wrongful trading requires different elements to be established

item.title: Recall Application u/r 11 Cannot be Utilised as Camouflage to Seek Review of an Order Decided on Merits: NCLAT [Read Order]
item.description: Dismissing the appeal of the appellant, the Tribunal clarified that Rule 11 preserves inherent powers only for correcting procedural errors or preventing abuse of process, not for reopening substantive findings.

item.title: Relief for Vodafone West Ltd: ITAT Deletes Addition on Trade Discount, Rules Trade Discount to Prepaid Distributors is Not 'Commission' [Read Order]
item.description: The tribunal held that a cellular mobile service provider is not under a legal obligation to deduct tax at source on the income or profit component in the payment received by distributors or franchisees from 3rd party customers.

item.title: S.19 of Contempt of Courts Act Limited to Punishment Orders: NCLAT Rejects Appeal Against Dismissal of Contempt [Read Order]
item.description: The Tribunal clarified that mere dismissal of contempt petitions does not fall within the appellate scope of Section 19. While acknowledging Section 425 of the Companies Act, 2013 confers contempt powers on NCLT and NCLAT, the Bench noted that the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code (IBC) does not expressly incorporate these provisions, leaving their applicability in insolvency proceedings unresolved.
